chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in Ihram who sleeps on his face on his wrapping garment. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.زَامِلَتِهِ: His wrapping garment or saddle-cloth (used as a cover)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to sleep on their face?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sleeping on one's face does not invalidate Ihram, distinguishing natural coverage from deliberate head-covering. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that minor, incidental covering of the face during sleep does not incur the penalty associated with intentional concealment. It serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims, ensuring that natural movements during rest do not disrupt the sanctity of their ritual state.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam sleeping upon his face on his wrapping’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Urn ay r from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who in the state of Ihram sleeps with a Zamilah (wrapping) on his face. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
